extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, botanists, plant anatomists, and physicians (readers of the Royal Society / Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and reporting a phytological (plant) natural history and anatomical study, especially of roots: what to observe, how to investigate (microscopy, anatomy, contents, principles, environment), and how to present results (figures, explanations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Particular and comparative survey of external vegetative characters
rubrics_metrics.description: a particular and comparative Gurvey of what relates to the more external consideration about vegetables; as of their figures, proportions, seasons, places, motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey external morphology and ecology: form, proportions, seasonal behaviour, habitats, movements; compare across taxa to identify commonalities and distinctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical survey of organical parts (with and without microscope)
rubrics_metrics.description: a like survey of the organical parts by anatomy, and how that is 'to be prosecuted, both without and with a microscope ; from thence we may come to know, what the communities of vegetables are as belonging to all; vi'hat their distinctions to such a kind ; their properties to such a species ; and their particularities to such particular ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out systematic anatomy to determine organs and tissues; use both naked-eye dissection and microscopy to resolve tissue structure and to infer characters at levels of genus, species, and individual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of the contents (fluids, secretions, chemical constituents)
rubrics_metrics.description: another similar survey of the contents of vegetables; of their several kinds, as spirits, airs and vapors, clear saps, milks, oils, gums, sugars, salts, &c. examined in all manner of ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate internal chemical/physical contents (saps, milks, oils, gums, sugars, salts, vapors) using varied methods; catalog and compare contents across organs and species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of the principles of organical parts (functional principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: a like survey of the principles as well as the contents of the organical parts. Whence will be attainable a further knowledge of the modes of vegetation, and of the sensible natures of vegetables, as also of their more recluse faculties and powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek underlying functional principles (physiological/causal factors) in organs to explain modes of vegetation and hidden faculties; connect structure and contents to function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey of external bodies and environment influencing vegetation
rubrics_metrics.description: a like survey of those bodies, either from which these principles are derived, or wherewith they have any communion; which are earth, and all solid receptacles; water, and all liquid receptacles; air and sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study soils, substrates, water regimes, air and light as sources or mediators of plant principles; include environmental measurements and their relation to plant structure/function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synthesize how principles assemble into a vegetable body (overarching question)
rubrics_metrics.description: In what manner these principles are so adapted as to become capable of being assembled together in such a number, connection, proportion and union, as to make a vegetable body?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose and address integrative questions about how materials, principles and parts combine quantitatively and structurally to produce whole organisms; aim for mechanistic synthesis grounded in prior surveys.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the skin of roots: origin, external accidents, and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The skin, its external accidents and original, its compounding parts, the one parenchymous, consisting of bubbles, the other ligneous, consisting of tubulary vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe epidermal/outer root tissues: developmental origin, external features (accidents), and subcomponents (parenchymatous bubble-like tissue vs ligneous tubular vessels); document with microscopy where useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study the bark: origin, external accidents, and compounding parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The bark; its original and external accidents, its compounding parts, likewise parenchymous, and ligneous; which latter consists of succiferous vessels, conjoined in threads, but no where inosculated, nor ramified, but distinct as the fibres of a nerve, which vessels are of various kinds, denominated from their contents, as lymphaeducts, lacteals, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine bark structure and composition (parenchyma and ligneous elements); identify and name vessel types by contents (e.g., succiferous, lymphatic, lacteal), note their arrangement (thread-like, non-ramified) and compare to animal tissues when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine root interior (within bark): composition and ligneous part
rubrics_metrics.description: That portion of the root within the bark, of the like composition with the former, and its ligneous part, compounded of succiferous and air-vessels. Where the structure of the bark, and more visibly of this portion of the root, is compared with that of a muscle; and the air-vessels with nerves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize inner root tissues: composition, presence of succiferous and air-vessels; use analogies (muscle, nerves) carefully to interpret structure and function; document spatial arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the pith: origin, parenchymous nature, texture and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: The pith, not common to all roots; its origin, parenchymous nature, and texture, like to a rete mirabile, of an infinite number of small fibres admirably complicated together; its contents being sometimes a limpid liquor, sometimes a vaporous air.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report whether pith is present, its developmental origin, parenchymatous fibrous architecture, and variable contents (liquid or gaseous); illustrate microscopic appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground vegetational account of roots on preceding anatomy and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: an account of the vegetation of roots, grounded chiefly on the foregoing anatomy. Where our author considers nature as one universal monarchy, visible in vegetables, if we take notice, that the soil is prepared by rain, sun, wind, air, and their several successions; that the parenchyma of the bark of the root, standing in the soil thus prepared, receives the watery parts of the soil, that the skin strains the water, and renders it more pure ; that the sap thus strained, yet being compounded of heterogeneous parts, and they received into the said parenchyma, they will now ferment; whereby being yet further prepared, they will more easily insinuate themselves into all the bubbles of that parenchyma...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain root growth and function by integrating anatomical structure with environmental preparation (soil/weather) and processes such as uptake, filtration by skin, fermentation/processing of sap, and movement through parenchyma; make mechanistic links between environment, tissue structure, and vegetative processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain a range of vegetative phenomena mechanistically
rubrics_metrics.description: explanation of a great variety of phaenomena, occurring in the contemplation of vegetables; as why the organical parts are void of taste, smell and colour : whence the succiferous vessels are tough, and the parenchymous parts friable? how the said succiferous vessels grow in length, cylindrical and hollow; the lactiferous how and why wider? how the air-vessels are formed? how the parenchymous parts become fibrous, and the fibres disposed into bubbles, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide mechanistic explanations for observable phenomena (sensory qualities, tissue toughness/fragility, vessel morphogenesis, air-vessel formation, parenchyma-to-fiber transformations), linking anatomy, composition and processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sensory descriptions and illustrated figures with explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: concluded with excellent observations of the odours of vegetables, of their colours and tastes; and the whole piece illustrated with 7 tables of cuts, representing the figures of several roots, as the author had viewed them, both with the naked eye and the microscope; together with an explication of these figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document organoleptic properties (odour, colour, taste) and provide illustrative plates (views by naked eye and microscope) with explanatory captions/interpretation; illustrations should support anatomical and physiological claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value simplicity, shortness, and generality in mathematical constructions (methodological criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Praises for constructions that are 'very simple and ingenious', 'a shorter can hardly be found', and constructions 'which obtains in all cases'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing or producing geometric/mathematical solutions, prefer constructions that are simple, concise, and applicable across cases; favor unifying analyses that subsume many special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer unifying analytical methods that yield many constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: observations that many different constructions and equations are 'contained in one and the same general analysis' and that the general analysis 'comprehends also infinite other constructions'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek general analytic frameworks that can generate multiple specific constructions/solutions rather than ad hoc case-by-case methods; emphasize unification and explanatory power.
